items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: I'm sure it was Les Paul, because he would come to the jam sessions someplace down in Morningside

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah. And, this was when I met -- let's see, Tyree was living at Ms. Waters' apartment, you

know, Tyree Glenn, that is, and Don Byas was, but I went there and met Freddie Green, and that's -- at that time, Les Paul, I think it was -- Les? Yeah, I think it was Les ... he was big in radio in New York, I think. I'm sure it was Les Paul, because he would come to the jam sessions someplace down in Morningside; a place they used to go down under, almost underground, and that was the first time that I went there, and Jimmy Mundy was getting ready to form a band, also.

You know, Jimmy Mundy was going to form a band, and I stayed there -- and I would go to every -- I played all over New York, going in jamming. I remember, you know, you hear of all these drummers; you're from the West Coast, and they never did talk too much about West Coast musicians at the time, because they thought -- they had the reputation of being good readers, but they didn't think that West Coast musicians could improvise, or [tad taoud] (PHONETIC) as they called it, right?
